events.title: Hagia Sophia Is Consecrated
events.description: Emperor Justinian I presided over the dedication of the rebuilt Hagia Sophia in Constantinople. The great domed cathedral had been finished in under six years, after the earlier church burned down during the Nika riots.
events.significance: The building changed the course of architecture with its enormous dome. It served as a cathedral, a mosque and a museum, and it remains one of the world's most recognizable landmarks.

events.title: Charles Darwin Sets Sail on HMS Beagle
events.description: The young naturalist Charles Darwin left Plymouth aboard HMS Beagle on a survey expedition that circled the globe. The voyage lasted almost five years.
events.significance: Darwin's observations of wildlife and geology on the voyage, especially in the Galápagos Islands, shaped his later theory of evolution by natural selection.

events.title: Apollo 8 Splashes Down
events.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and William Anders returned safely to Earth. They splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon.
events.significance: The mission showed that humans could travel to the Moon and return. It also produced the famous 'Earthrise' photograph, and it paved the way for the Apollo 11 landing in 1969.

events.title: Soviet Forces Seize Control in Afghanistan
events.description: Soviet troops moved into Kabul. President Hafizullah Amin was ousted and killed in a coup backed by Moscow.
events.significance: The coup began a Soviet–Afghan war that lasted more than a decade. The war reshaped Cold War politics and left lasting effects on Afghanistan and the wider region.
